newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila central bank eyes more overnight rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Manila central bank eyes more overnight rate cuts.

text.p: The Philippine central bank said on Sunday it hoped to make further cuts in the overnight borrowing rate if the currency market continued to stabilise.
It added that the rate could return to single digit levels in a few weeks.

The central bank slashed the rate twice last week after effectively devaluing the peso. The latest cut on Friday took the rate down to 25 percent. Ahead of last week's reductions, the rate stood at 32 percent.

"Next week, if the market normalises some more, we will cut it again and hopefully in a few weeks, that will go back to normal," central bank governor Gabriel Singson said in an interview on private radio station DZRH.
Asked what he meant by normal, Singson said: "The overnight rate before was low, single digit."
Asked about reports that some people might have benefited from the fall of the peso, Singson said:

"We have certain circulars that the banks should have limits on their dollar holdings to not more than 20 percent of their unencumbered capital. If we will find out in our examination that any bank has exceeded this limit then we will impose the sanction."
Singson called on people not to panic, saying the country had weathered currency jolts in the past.
He cited a case in 1990 when the Philippines devalued the peso to 28.00 from 25.75 against the dollar, and again in 1993 when the rate floated up to 29.83.
The problem with Filipinos was "we panic easily," he said.
He said the peso, which closed unchanged at 28.00 on Friday, was "still stabilising down."
"Me, I did not lose sleep because I have seen this too many times in the past," he said.
Singson, a golfer, said he even almost scored a hole-in-one during the peso crisis, "just an inch from the cup."
